subject: Seeking help with piecewise fitted lines via stat_curve(),  stat_function(), or stat_smooth()

messages.author: be361c3feab6dc4c
messages.subject: Seeking help with piecewise fitted lines via stat_curve(),  stat_function(), or stat_smooth()
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to plot some fitted lines in a piecewise fashion with
ggplot. I usually use curve(), but I can't find any documentation on
stat_curve() [a.k.a., geom_curve()] other than this:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/28cfd766277c6c71/b0ea4c53e16c42c7?lnk=gst&q=geom_curve#b0ea4c53e16c42c7

In the absence of documentation about stat_curve(), I have tried to
use stat_function() and stat_smooth() without success (see
reproducible example below).

Thanks in advance for any help you can provide.

Regards,
Chris


#Reproducible example

#Simulate outcomes from a regression discontinuity design.
set.seed(100)
x <- rnorm(200, 0, 10)
z <- ifelse(x<0, 1, 0)
tx <- which(z==1)
set.seed(101)
y <- rnorm(200, 50, 10) + 10*z + 0.5*x - 0.025*x^2

#Fit a regression discontinuity model.
model <- lm(y ~ z + x + I(x^2))
coefs <- coefficients(model)

#Plot fitted lines.
plot(y ~ x, col=NULL, ylim=c(min(y)-10, max(y)+10))
abline(v=0, lty=2, lwd=2, col="darkgrey")
points(x[tx], y[tx], col="darkgrey", pch=4)
points(x[-tx], y[-tx], col="darkgrey")
curve(coefs[1] + coefs[2] + coefs[3]*x + coefs[4]*x^2, min(x)-10, 0,
add=T)
curve(coefs[1] + coefs[3]*x + coefs[4]*x^2, 0, max(x)+10, add=T)

#Attempt to plot fitted lines with ggplot.
data.plot <- data.frame(x, y, z)
g1 <- ggplot(data.plot, aes(y=y, x=x)) +
geom_point(aes(shape=factor(z)), color="darkgrey") +
scale_shape_manual(name="Treatment", value=c(1, 4)) +
opts(legend.position="none")
funk <- function(x) coefs[1] + coefs[2]*ifelse(x<0, 1, 0) + coefs[3]*x
+ coefs[4]*x^2
g1 + stat_function(fun=funk) #undesired line segment spanning local
average treatment effect
g1 + stat_function(fun=funk, data=data.plot[which(data.plot$z==1),])
#undesired line segment spanning local average treatment effect and
extending beyond cutoff
g1 + stat_function(fun=funk, data=data.plot[which(data.plot$z==0),])
#undesired line segment spanning local average treatment effect and
extending beyond cutoff
g1 + stat_smooth(method="lm", se=F, formula=formula(model)) #Error in
model.frame.default(Terms, newdata, na.action = na.action, xlev =
object$xlevels) : variable lengths differ (found for 'x') In addition:
Warning message: 'newdata' had 80 rows but variable(s) found have 200
rows
g1 + stat_smooth(method="lm", se=F, formula=formula(model),
fullrange=F, data=data.plot[which(data.plot$z==1),]) #Error in
model.frame.default(formula = formula, data = data, weights =
weight, : variable lengths differ (found for 'z')
g1 + stat_smooth(method="lm", se=F, formula=formula(model),
fullrange=F, data=data.plot[which(data.plot$z==0),]) #Error in
model.frame.default(formula = formula, data = data, weights =
weight, : variable lengths differ (found for 'z')

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Seeking help with piecewise fitted lines via stat_curve(),  stat_function(), or stat_smooth()
parts:
Hi:

Try this:

f1 <- function(x) ifelse(x <= 0, coefs[1] + coefs[2] + coefs[3] * x + coefs[4] * x^2, NA)
f2 <- function(x) ifelse(x > 0, coefs[1] + coefs[3] * x + coefs[4] * x^2, NA)
g1 + stat_function(fun = f1) + stat_function(fun = f2)

It's an ugly hack, but it seems to work for this example. The graph isn't perfect because the first curve doesn't plot exactly at zero, but that must be something in the curve rendering algorithm because f1 is defined at x = 0.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Seeking help with piecewise fitted lines via stat_curve(),  stat_function(), or stat_smooth()
parts:
Hi Dennis, Chris,

As always, for more complicated models, I'd recommend computing the
data yourself:

pred <- ddply(data.plot, "z", function(df) {
x <- seq(min(df$x), max(df$x), length = 20)
newdata <- data.frame(x, z = df$z[1])

data.frame(x, y = predict(model, newdata = newdata))
})

ggplot(data.plot, aes(x, y)) +
geom_point(aes(shape = factor(z))) +
geom_line(aes(group = z), data = pred) +
geom_vline(xintercept = 0)

Hadley
